metadata.encoding: Coordinates are integers: (lon - origin lon) x scale, (lat - origin lat) x scale. Lines and rings are flat [x, y, x, y...] arrays, each pair a delta from the previous one.

sources.old_network: Vasserot cadastre, street space (ALPAGE via Stanford Libraries, ODbL), about 1836
sources.pavements_crossings_bollards: Ville de Paris, plan de voirie (Paris Data, ODbL)
sources.lamps: Ville de Paris, éclairage public (Paris Data, ODbL)
sources.fountains_kiosks: Ville de Paris, fontaines à boire and kiosques de presse (Paris Data, ODbL)

central_gutter.note: Old Paris streets were cambered toward a central gutter (ruisseau) and had no pavements. Shown on every street of the 1836 network between 2.4 and 14 m wide, until the Haussmann clearances (1860, as the model).

old_pavements.note: Prefect Chabrol required granite-kerbed pavements on new streets from 1823; the law of 7 June 1845 and the Paris arrêté of 1846 made them general. Approximation: streets of the 1836 network at least 10 m wide get 1.6 m pavements from 1845.

modern_network.note: Today's pavements and crossings (plan de voirie) from 1860, when Haussmann's works rebuilt the Cité; streets that survived (around rue Chanoinesse) switch from the old network then too (approximation).

bridge_pavements.note: Pavements over the river are shown from the year the present bridge was built (BRIDGE_YEARS).

oil_lanterns.note: Réverbères (oil lamps with reflectors, from 1766-1769) hung on a rope across the street. Gas replaced oil from 1839; by the early 1850s oil was left only on secondary streets, and the six gas companies merged in 1855. Approximation for the Cité: gas from 1850. Spacing: one every 45 m (12,761 burners lit Paris in 1788, three or four per lantern).

gas_lamps.note: Gas lanterns on wall brackets in narrow streets and on cast-iron candelabra elsewhere. On the modern network they stand at today's lamp positions. The last gas lamps of Paris went out in 1962; functional electric poles are shown from 1960 where today's lamp is functional (approximation).

stone_plaques.note: Street names engraved on stone tablets at street corners, ordered in 1728 and put up from 1729.

enamel_plaques.note: Blue enamelled plaques with white letters, decided under Rambuteau and put up from 1847.

rambuteau_columns.note: Colonnes Rambuteau: urinals inside a column carrying posters, authorised in 1839 (478 by 1841). Only on pavements, so from 1845 on the old network.

morris_columns.note: Gabriel Morris's poster columns, from 1868. No dataset gives positions: placed on wide pavements about 180 m apart.

vespasiennes.note: Cast-iron urinals that replaced the Rambuteau columns from 1868; replaced in turn by automatic toilets from 1980 (approximation). Placed about 300 m apart on wide pavements.

kiosks.note: Newspaper kiosks from 1857 (Davioud). Today's kiosks (Paris Data), shown from 1860 at their present places.

wallace_fountains.note: Wallace fountains from 1872. Today's fountains (Paris Data, type FONTNE_WALLACE), shown from 1872 at their present places; the dataset has no installation dates.

benches.note: Davioud's double benches came with the promenades of the Second Empire. Placed every 35 m or so on pavements at least 4.5 m deep (approximation).

kerb_stones.note: Stone bollards (bornes, chasse-roues) guarded the corners of houses on the old streets. Placed at block corners of the 1836 network.

bollards.note: Today's cast-iron bollards (plan de voirie). Shown from 1980 (approximation: anti-parking bollards spread in the 1970s and 1980s).

crossings.note: Today's pedestrian crossings (plan de voirie). Studded crossings (passages cloutés) from 1930 (78 in Paris in 1928, over 12,000 in 1934); white bars from 1963 (interministerial instruction of 22 October 1963).

centre_lines.note: Dashed centre lines on two-way main roads from 1963 (same instruction; approximation).

road_surfaces.note: Drawn by the ground shader by year: sandstone setts until the 1960s (in 1907 about 6 of Paris's 10 million m² of roadway were still sandstone); main roads macadam from 1860 and asphalt from 1900 (asphalt first laid in rue Bergère in 1854); asphalt everywhere from 1970, as setts were tarred over after 1968 (approximations).

items.note: One row per type and life; xy is a flat delta-encoded list, angle_deg and param give one value per item (or are empty when all are 0).
